To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) second order queries can be used as a query language for ontological data access, (ii) second order rewriting is a useful technique to decide query entailment for rule based data access, and (iii) second order rewriting can be combined with forward chaining to achieve decidability of query entailment

(1) we introduce a new query formalism based on MSO logic, (2) we show that this formalism subsumes the query formalism of DL-Lite and Datalog+, and that it is more expressive than conjunctive queries, (3) we propose rewriting algorithms that transform a rule set into a query in this formalism, (4) we show that the query entailment problem for a rule set is decidable if the rule set is rewritable and has the

(i) the new formalism is expressive and has a decidable entailment problem, (ii) the formalism can be combined with existing rule based formalisms, (iii) query rewriting can be used to decide entailment for most of the existing approaches and (iv) query rewriting can even be used for query answering in the new formalism
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new formalism, new algorithms and new techniques for query rewriting in rule based data access.
a formalism that is expressive and decidable, that allows for a query rewriting approach, and that can be implemented efficiently by a bottom up algorithm.
a novel approach to rule based query rewriting and query entailment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we can answer all first order queries and a large subset of second order queries with our approach.

the query rewriting method is a powerful and general method for deciding rule entailment, and the bottom up computation method is a powerful method for computing rule entailment, but the combination of the two methods is a powerful and practical method for deciding and answering queries.
the query entailment problem is decidable for all the rule based approaches considered in this work.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that second order queries can be used to capture the expressivity and the complexity of the rule based data access paradigm.
we provide the theoretical basis for answering second order queries in rule based data management.
we show how second order query rewriting can be used to extend the expressivity of query rewriting for rule sets that are not rewritable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of these two techniques allows us to answer a wide class of queries in a rule based setting, and that it can be done efficiently.
second order queries can be used to express a rich class of conjunctive queries that are beyond the reach of first order queries.
query rewriting is a viable technique for answering second order queries under constraints expressed by a rich class of rule languages.
